name: Forehand push
summary: A controlled backspin return on the forehand side, stepping in for short balls.
whenToUse: Against short backspin to your forehand when the ball is too low or short to attack.

keyPoints.stance: Step in toward the ball with your right foot (left-handers: left foot), under the table for short balls.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Lean in from the hips; the body stays quiet.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Short: forward and slightly down, finishing toward the target.
keyPoints.timing: Early, at or just before the top of the bounce.
keyPoints.freeArm: Out to the side or resting near the table edge for balance.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow bent, forearm guides the bat forward. Bat face open, contact under the back of the ball.
keyPoints.recovery: Push off the front foot and step back to ready straight away.
keyPoints.anticipation: Short balls to the forehand often come from a serve. Watch the server's bat to judge the spin.

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player step in and push. Notice the foot goes first.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: step in, push, step out.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did your foot step in before the bat moved?
Did you push off back to ready?

learningPath.task: First contact with slow backspin to your forehand.
Forehand push rally until 20 in a row.
Receive with pushes from both wings.
Play points where you must push the first short ball.
learningPath.passCheck: Win 3 points after a good push.

learningPath.task: Test: forehand pushes in a row.

gamePatterns.situation: A short backspin serve to your forehand.
gamePatterns.how: Step in and push it long to their backhand, or drop it short if they stand far back.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent drops the ball short in a push rally.
gamePatterns.how: Step in early and push long to a corner so they have to move.

fixes: Step under the table with your playing-side foot

troubleshooting.symptom: I'm stuck at the table after the push
fixes: Push off the front foot after contact

penholdNotes: Penholders often find the forehand push natural; keep the wrist from over-turning so the ball stays low.
